page.layout: One page of text, one column, with a running head at the top. Below the text, a catchword at the right margin. No margin notes.

main_text.head: Quid est Vocalis?
main_text.p: Vocalis est litera, quæ per se syllabam potest effi-cere: ut,a,e,i,o,u,y.
main_text.head: Quid est Consona?
main_text.p: Consona est litera, quæ tantùm cum vocali sylla-bâ potest efficere,ut literæ omnes,præter sex vocales.
main_text.head: Quomodo dividitur Consona?
main_text.p: In mutam, liquidam, & duplicem. Octo consonæ sunt mutæ: ut,b,c,d,f,g,p,q,t. Quatuor sunt liquidæ: ut,l,m,n,r. Tres sunt duplices: ut,x,z, & jod, quoties inter duas vocales ponitur: ut,pejor,major.
main_text.head: Observatio.
main_text.p: Etsi scribimus Cneus & Cajus; tamen Gneus & Gajus secundùm Grammaticos pronuntiamus.
main_text.head: Quid est Syllaba?
main_text.p: Syllaba est unius litera, aut multarum comprehen-sio, uno eodemq; spiritu ac tono proferenda: ut,a,e, i,o,u,y, æ,œ,au,eu,ei,ab,ars,mars,stans,stirps. Dua-rum vocalium in unam syllabam comprehensus so-nus Diphthongus appellatur. Veteres Diphthogum ei, ufurparunt in pluralibus masculinis & fœmininis Accusativis nominum, quæ ium habent in genitivo plurali: ut,acreis,omneis,salubreis,parteis,arteis.
Hactenus de litera & syllaba dictum est: sequuntur affectiones omnibus vocibus communes, videlicet Species & Figura.
main_text.head: Quid est Species Vocis?
main_text.p: Species vocis est,qua disquiritur,utrùm vox sit Pri-mitiva,an Derivativa. Primitiva est, quæ à nulla alia descendit: ut,Equus,ein pferd/Aper,ein wilde schwein. Derivativa est,quæ ab alia voce originem trahit: ut, Equuleus, ein Füllen/Aprugnus, vo wilden schwein.

page.notes: The German glosses "ein pferd", "ein wilde schwein", "ein Füllen", "vo wilden schwein" are set in black letter inside the roman text; they were transcribed in roman form with the printed spelling kept. "Aprugnus, vo wilden schwein" likely reads "vo" as printed; the first gloss in the Primitiva line is uncertain. Diphthogum (ei) and "Veteres Diphthogum" are printed as such. The catchword "Quid" is at the bottom right. Spelling is kept as printed: long s appears as "s" in the Latin headings and text, though the rule requires a plain s; the transcription should be checked against that rule.
